review.title: Retry provider requests after transient failures
review.author: dev-example
reviewed_scope: payment submission and retry call path

decision.rationale: The retry path can create a second charge after a lost response because requests are not idempotent.

summary: The initial review found that an ambiguous transport failure can retry a completed payment without a stable idempotency key.

findings.title: Lost-response retries can submit the same payment twice
findings.observation: The retry loop creates a new provider request on each attempt and does not reuse an idempotency key.
findings.trigger: The provider accepts the first charge, but the client loses the response and classifies the transport error as retryable.
findings.impact: The same customer operation can produce two provider charges and inconsistent reconciliation state.

evidence.description: Each loop iteration constructs a request without a stable idempotency identifier.

findings.remediation: Use one stable provider idempotency key for every attempt of the same logical payment.
findings.verification: Simulate an accepted request followed by a transport error and prove every attempt uses the same payment-scoped key.

required_actions.action: Make provider retries idempotent and add a lost-response regression test.

risks.description: Ambiguous retry outcomes can create duplicate charges.

reviewer_runs.environment: Node.js 22 on Linux; no provider network access
reviewer_runs.summary: Existing retry tests passed; no lost-response scenario was present.

ci_checks.name: unit-tests
ci_checks.summary: Repository unit tests passed for the previous head.

limitations: Provider sandbox behavior and production request logs were unavailable.
open_questions: Does the provider guarantee idempotency when one payment key is reused across retries?
assumptions: A transport error can occur after the provider has accepted the request.
